title: Scalar triple product and volume
section: Analytic Geometry of R3 ▷ The Triple Scalar Product
terms: scalar triple product; parallelepiped; coplanarity; oriented volume; tetrahedron volume; Gram determinant.

exposition.text:
The scalar triple product (u × v) · w equals the determinant whose rows are u, v, w. Its abso-
lute value is the volume of their parallelepiped, while its sign records orientation. Cyclically
permuting the three inputs preserves the value; swapping two negates it.
The triple product vanishes exactly when the vectors are linearly dependent, equivalently when
their directions lie in a common plane. A tetrahedron with vertices P, Q, R, S has volume |((Q −
P) × (R − P)) · (S − P)|/6. Always use displacement vectors from one common vertex; raw
position vectors work only when that vertex is the origin.
If G is the Gram matrix G = v · v of three vectors, their squared scalar triple product is det G:

question.text:
What is the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices (1, 0, 0), (1, 2, 0), (1, 0, 3), (5, 1, 1)?
(A) 2 (B) 3 (C) 4 (D) 8 (E) 24

solution.text:
The displacement vectors are (0, 2, 0), (0, 0, 3), (4, 1, 1). Their scalar triple product is (6, 0, 0) ·
(4, 1, 1) = 24. Divide by 6 to obtain 4.

question.text:
Vectors u, v have lengths 2, 3 and make angle π/6. Among vectors w of length 4, what is the
largest possible parallelepiped volume |(u × v) · w|?
√ √
(A) 6 (B) 12 (C) 12 3 (D) 24 (E) 24 3

solution.text:
The base parallelogram has area ∥u × v∥ = 2 · 3 sin(π/6) = 3. Its perpendicular height is at
most ∥w∥ = 4, with equality when w is parallel to u × v. Thus the maximum volume is 12.
